column1: # DP-1523 audit — every strconv.Atoi call under pkg/ (non-test), one row per call.
#   go_site            Go file:line of the call
#   c_site             src/ site it ports (read this session, R5g), or — when C has no counterpart
#   c_parse            what C uses there: atoi / strtol / sscanf / is_number+atoi / fscanf / —
#   why                one line; overflow = input of >18 digits that (int)strtol wraps/saturates
# Player-typed numbers C reads with atoi == (int)strtol: skip leading isspace, optional
# sign, stop at first non-digit; overflow clamps to LONG_MIN/LONG_MAX then keeps the low
# rejects trailing junk and errors on overflow, so every player-input atoi port below
# diverges on digit-leading junk and/or huge tokens until switched to common.AtoiC.

column5: why

column1: # --- wizard load/vstat: fixed in this PR (the two witnessed DP-1523 reds) ---

column5: FIXED: loadAtoi (wiz_object.go:128-138 on origin/main) returned 0 on Atoi error so "load obj 99999999999999999999" created a bug; C atoi wraps to -1 and answers "A NEGATIVE number??".
FIXED: strconv.Atoi error answered the usage line; C atoi wraps to -1 and answers "A NEGATIVE number??" for both obj and mob branches.

column1: # --- wizard movement class (follow-up batch: needs C-first red scenario) ---

column5: parseSignedIntPrefix serves dig, dc and advance: its digit run only fails Atoi on >int64 input, where C atoi wraps (dig room, dc desc_num, advance level all take the wrapped value).
parseLeadingInt feeds goto/at: overflow wrap can land on a valid vnum (e.g. 2^32+N) that Go refuses with "No room exists with that number.".

column1: # --- who/users class (follow-up batch; C parses ranges with sscanf, not atoi) ---

column5: users -l range low: sscanf stops at junk and wraps overflow through int; Atoi rejects both, so "users -l 5abc-10" diverges.
users -l range high, same class.
who level range low (parseWhoLevelRange): same sscanf-vs-Atoi class.
who level range high, same class.
who space-separated upper extension: deliberate port addition on top of the sscanf divergences above.
who -l space-separated upper, same.
Board read: C atoi("5abc") is 5 and overflow wraps negative into the "That message exists only in your imagination." arm; Go refuses and shows the board instead.
Board remove: same class as read.
Board /e line edit: C atoi overflow answers "Line number must be higher than 0."; Go swallows the line silently on Atoi error.
